Timeline::weekday¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::weekday() const

weekday() is the sole public spelling.

Number The Days From Monday¶

weekday() maps each local date to an int32 code using this exact convention:

Day

Code

Monday

0

Tuesday

1

Wednesday

2

Thursday

3

Friday

4

Saturday

5

Sunday

6

The method is elementwise and shape-preserving. An absent instant maps to -1, which is outside the valid weekday range.

Example: Verify The Numbering Convention¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2020-12-31T23:59:59.123456789Z",
    "2021-01-01T00:00:00.987654321Z",
    "2024-02-29T06:07:08.009010011Z",
    "",
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, events.weekday());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[3, 4, 3, -1]

Both 31 December 2020 and 29 February 2024 were Thursdays, hence 3.

Building Calendar Rules¶

For a generic numeric feature, weekday() is compact and easy to compare. For intent-revealing predicates, use methods such as is_monday(), is_weekend(), or is_business_day(). For presentation text, use weekday_name() rather than maintaining a parallel label table.

All of these methods evaluate the local date. Convert to the operating timezone before classifying a timestamp that lies near midnight.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Monday is 0; Sunday is 6.

  • weekday() is different from day() and dayofyear().

  • Weekend and business-day policy should use the dedicated predicates rather than embedding numeric codes throughout application logic.

  • -1 identifies NaT, not an eighth weekday.
